company: Blue Storm Associates Inc. (dba PEMDAS Technologies & Innovations)
dod_intent_evidence: Navy 2023 sequential SBIR Phase II DMO-EI ($1.5M), $49.5M Air National Guard environmental-intelligence IDIQ (2017), EI suite deployed at Arctic Edge 2025 — sbir_abstract, news, and homepage sections.
score_evidence: "Revolutionary Technologies" and "ground breaking research" marketing gloss, but paired with "radar-denied, data-sparse Arctic environment" operational framing → lab_language_intensity kept low

"delivering critical atmospheric intelligence in a radar-denied, data-sparse Arctic environment. These capabilities directly supported UAS and real-world mission operations" → deployment_awareness_absence low — they demonstrably operate in degraded environments
"provide real threat warnings and displays to pilots and operators" and 80% veterans employed → operator_absence very low
No jobs data in pack → hiring_profile_skew set exactly 10 per rule
Sequential Phase II awarded 2023 — the transition clock on DMO-EI is running now

blind_spots.blind_spot: DMO-EI promises real-time machine-to-machine weather push to distributed maritime platforms — the one fleet that fights radio-silent
blind_spots.operator_reality: Distributed Maritime Operations doctrine is EMCON: ships and unmanned platforms minimize RF emissions and connectivity, so 'real-time cloud and icing layers' delivered over live links is exactly the data path a contested Pacific fight denies — the frame-rate-decoupling problem in weather form
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's fluency is atmospheric science and cockpit display integration; the abstract specifies products and altitudes but never an EMCON/DDIL delivery architecture
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The prototype DMO-EI will employ machine-to-machine processing to derive Navy mission decision products to improve success and enhance survivability.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Platform integration targets were still undetermined inside the Phase II period
blind_spots.operator_reality: "Determined based on availability of Navy/Marine Corps/Coast Guard assets" means the schedule's critical path is GFE access the company doesn't control — waiting on government aircraft availability is precisely how months-to-field exceeds funded months remaining
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Sequential-SBIR habit: prior Army effort supplied the pattern, so asset availability reads as an admin detail rather than the program-killing dependency it is
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The specific systems the prototype DMO-EI system will integrate will be determined based on availability of Navy/Marine Corps/Coast Guard assets.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Eight years of demos, exercises, and sequential SBIRs with no visible program of record or named transition sponsor
blind_spots.operator_reality: Arctic Edge and cockpit demos prove operators like it — but operators loving it is not adoption; without a resourced champion above the squadron level (PEO, program office, POM line) the EI suite stays an exercise guest, and each sequential SBIR restarts the clock
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Deep operator empathy (80% veterans) makes exercise success feel like traction; the advocacy-chain gap is invisible from inside the demo loop
blind_spots.evidence_quote: PEMDAS deployed its Environmental Intelligence (EI) suite during Arctic Edge 2025, delivering critical atmospheric intelligence in a radar-denied, data-sparse Arctic environment.

opener_hook: PEMDAS's DMO-EI Phase II promises real-time weather pushed machine-to-machine across a distributed fleet — the same fleet whose doctrine is EMCON, where real-time links are the first thing commanders turn off.
what_they_do: Veteran-heavy 47-person environmental-intelligence firm turning atmospheric sensing into cockpit and mission decision tools for DoD, cycling through SBIRs and exercises toward an elusive program of record.
